Australia. An island continent in the southern hemisphere, the world's sixth-largest country by area and the smallest continent, with a population of over twenty-six million concentrated on its coasts. Originally inhabited for at least sixty-five thousand years by Aboriginal Australians, Australia was colonized by Britain in seventeen eighty-eight and developed from a penal colony into a major developed nation.

Australia's interior, the Outback, is a vast arid region of deserts and grasslands. The most famous geographic features are Uluru, also called Ayers Rock, and the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system. Aboriginal Australians inhabited Australia for at least sixty-five thousand years, developing complex cultures, languages, and spiritual traditions before European contact. They comprise over three percent of modern Australia's population. Captain James Cook's voyage along the eastern coast in seventeen seventy led to British claims on the continent. Britain established a penal colony at Port Jackson in seventeen eighty-eight, which grew into Sydney.

Australia's White Australia Policy from nineteen zero one to the nineteen seventies restricted non-European immigration, reflecting racist attitudes that marginalized Aboriginal Australians and created homogeneous Anglo-European settlement. The Great Barrier Reef, stretching twenty-three hundred kilometers along Queensland's coast, is the world's largest coral reef system and one of the seven natural wonders of the world. It is threatened by climate change. Australia played a crucial role in the Pacific Theater of World War Two, serving as a base for the Allies' campaign against Japan.

The Sydney Opera House opened in nineteen seventy-three, designed by Danish architect Jorn Utzon. It is an iconic modernist building and one of the world's most recognizable structures. Aboriginal Dreamtime stories and dot painting art traditions represent one of humanity's oldest continuing artistic traditions, spanning tens of thousands of years.
